label: <DEL> step of long sequences that begin with b/g/w/a/j/v
explanation: Fires almost only on the <DEL> delimiter step: 99.95% of activations, 6 stray original-phase steps, never in the copy phase. It fires on 12.9% of delimiter steps. Within the delimiter step it acts like a graded sum of two things. (1) Sequence length: the rate rises steeply with L, from 0.2% at L=3-5 to 16% at L=9, and L>=8 holds 81% of the mass. (2) Identity of the first original token, i.e. the token about to be output: b, g, w, a, j and v have 4-7x lift, and the second original token adds a smaller, similar contribution. The top activations (about 0.19-0.20) are L=8-9 sequences starting b w / b j / w a. A rule of L>=7 plus first or second token in {b,g,w,a,j,v} gets dev F1 0.56 with mass recall 0.78. Misses are mostly weak activations on shorter sequences or with other leading tokens; false positives are long sequences with a matching token that stay just below threshold. Because the behaviour is graded and distributed, no crisp predicate goes past about 0.58 F1.
